note: post hoc profiled attack, not a pre-registered criterion; key rank = number of wrong guesses scored above the correct one (ties count 1/2): 0 = recovered, 1.5 = random for 4 guesses; GE = mean key rank, SR = P(rank 0)

distinguishers.tmpl: primary: Gaussian template with pooled covariance on the default POIs (top ANOVA F, number chosen by cross-validation on the profiling rows); it compares the traces with the absolute level of the template means, so it sees a key bit's main effect
distinguishers.tmpl_bits: post hoc (added after stage-2 review B1): the same Gaussian template on 1-3 POIs, the top-F sample plus, for each key bit x1 and x2, the sample with the largest in-cell contrast of that bit (chi2 over the 16 cells of the other four bits), dropping a candidate within 3 samples of one already taken; profiling rows only
distinguishers.corr: secondary: correlation between the traces and the guess's template means, both centred per POI over the attack traces; limitation: the centring removes the level shift between keys, which is a key bit's main effect, so it cannot see a leak like N's (see the injection test)

method.k_poi_template_choice: 5-fold cross-validation on the profiling rows (blocks of 10 rows, guard 1); held-out information about x
method.poi_selection: top ANOVA F over the 32 inputs, profiling rows only
method.poi_selection_tmpl_bits: top-F sample plus the top in-cell contrast sample of key bit x1 and of x2, near-duplicates dropped; profiling rows only
method.null: profiling labels permuted independently per split, order, noise and draw; whole pipeline rerun; p_vs_null = (1 + #draws with GE <= real) / (draws + 1)
method.units: one (split, scenario) pair; GE/SR averaged over trials within a unit
method.ge_sem: standard error over the scenario means (splits averaged first; the splits reuse the same rows): 8 scenarios, 4 keys for U_cpa

injection.note: alpha x N's first-order leak (per-input mean pattern at N's top-F sample, in units of the within-input SD) added at one sample of the real traces; alpha = 1 is N's per-sample effect size; detected = final GE below every null draw of order1_noise0

alpha x N's first-order leak (per-input mean pattern at N's top-F sample, in units of the within-input SD) added at one sample of the real traces; alpha = 1 is N's per-sample effect size; detected = final GE below every null draw of order1_noise0

U_cpa.note: the CPA campaigns' neighbouring rows share the IV and key bits, so fewer input bits toggle than in U_tvla and the traces draw 18-27 % less charge than the templates predict; the Gaussian template (absolute level) suffers from this mismatch between campaigns, the centred correlation does not. At the final checkpoint every trace of a key is used, so each of the 4 keys is one deterministic outcome

statements.primary: The Gaussian template (tmpl) is the primary distinguisher; tmpl_bits is a post hoc variant of it with per-key-bit POIs; the correlation (corr) is secondary and cannot see a key bit's main effect.
statements.N: N, first order, 765 attack traces per key. Default template (POIs by overall F): GE 0.38, SR 0.62, P(x1) 1.00, P(x2) 0.63. Template with per-key-bit POIs (post hoc): GE 0.07, SR 0.93, P(x1) 1.00, P(x2) 0.93 (null GE 1.48 +- 0.09; p = 0.048).
statements.N_order2: Second order on N (template GE 0.05) is not independent evidence: the centred square at samples with a first-order mean shift carries that shift.
statements.D: D, first order, 521 attack traces per key: template GE 1.48 against a null of 1.51 +- 0.07 (20 permutations; p = 0.286). At this data volume the template detects an injected leak shaped like N's down to 0.35 x N's strength (GE 1.22), not at 0.25 x (GE 1.55); the correlation detects none of the injected leaks, not even at N's full strength (GE 1.49).
statements.DA: DA, first order, 533 attack traces per key: template GE 1.54 against a null of 1.50 +- 0.09 (20 permutations; p = 0.667). At this data volume the template detects an injected leak shaped like N's down to 0.5 x N's strength (GE 1.03), not at 0.35 x (GE 1.38) or 0.25 x (GE 1.58); the correlation detects none of the injected leaks, not even at N's full strength (GE 1.47).
statements.K1: Post hoc, a profiled attack on the K1 CPA traces (templates from U_tvla, no added noise): template SR >= 0.9 from 2 traces per key. This answers the question K1 was meant to settle, whether the traces carry exploitable key information, but K1 stays failed as registered.
statements.U_cpa_noise: With added noise, on all 1998 traces per key (4 keys, one outcome each): 0.5x noise: template GE 1.25 (SR 0.25), correlation GE 0.50 (SR 0.75); 1x noise: template GE 1.50 (SR 0.25), correlation GE 0.00 (SR 1.00). The CPA traces draw 18-27 % less charge than the U_tvla templates predict.
